messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — Multiple BGP peer flaps observed from upstream provider AS33211, affecting egress paths from NA regions. Auto-escalating to oncall. Please acknowledge. :rotating_light:
ashwin: acked. oncall here — looking at telemetry now. which POPs are showing the highest loss?
maria: SFO and IAD are showing rapid AS path churn, packet loss spikes ~18% to some prefixes. DNS resolution for some customer domains shows increased latency and occasional NXDOMAINs — could be due to our egress flipping to degraded providers.
nate: paging noc to confirm provider side. @noc can you reach out to provider NOC and confirm whether they are seeing a control-plane storm?
noc: pinged provider NOC (ticket 556732). They're seeing a surge in route withdrawals and re-announcements from a transit neighbor. Provider suspects a misconfiguration on their side but are still investigating.
jia: can we quickly fail traffic to alternate providers for affected prefixes? suggest prepending and lowering local preference for the flaky transit to force our egress to other peers.
ashwin: agreed — plan: 1) add AS-path prepend to routes via AS33211 for impacted prefixes, 2) temporarily divert DNS queries to secondary resolvers and enable EDNS fallback, 3) rate-limit session churn on our routers to avoid CPU spikes. I'll coordinate config changes.
alexa: tagging customer-ops for impact statement. initial telemetry: 2.4% of requests to hosted-api endpoints saw >500ms latency, SLO risk for a handful of customers in NA-West.
peering-team: standing by for signed-off commands. confirm which prefixes we modify — we should avoid changing _all_ egress to prevent downstream oscillation.
maria: list of top prefixes by traffic: 52.19.0.0/16, 34.201.0.0/16, 3.80.0.0/14. those 3 account for ~62% of affected egress in SFO.
nate: @peering-team go ahead to prepend 3x for AS33211 on those prefixes. keep community no-export? yes keep no-export unchanged.
peering-team: applying prepends now on SFO-facing routers:```
# config snippet (show run)
route-map PREPEND-AS33211 permit 10
 set as-path prepend 33211 33211 33211
!
router bgp 64000
 neighbor 203.0.113.45 route-map PREPEND-AS33211 out
```
peering-team: applied to SFO edge (sfo-rt-02), rolling to IAD in 2 min.
noc: provider confirms they see reduced incoming flaps after our prepends. they will keep watch.
ashwin: switching DNS resolvers for affected edge cache cluster to secondary upstreams and enabling EDNS fallback. command:```
# knot config diff
policy "egress-dns" {
  fallback-resolver = "8.8.8.8"
}
```
jia: monitoring: after changes packet loss on affected prefixes dropped from 18% -> 2.1% in SFO, latency normalizing. DNS NXDOMAIN reports down by ~85%.
maria: starting customer-impact post to status page draft: "We are investigating intermittent connectivity and DNS resolution issues impacting some customers in NA-West and NA-East due to upstream provider route instability. Mitigations applied; monitoring shows improvement. Root cause under investigation with provider."
alexa: post drafted, will wait for final wording. any customers to notify directly (enterprise contracts)?
nate: yes — pinging AE for top-10 impacted customers to prepare tailored notice.
peering-team: follow-up with provider: request they share BGP update dumps for the 15:23-15:35 window and ask for RCA timeline. also request they confirm whether this was an internal churn or a route leak from their peer.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation implemented: AS-path prepends + DNS fallback. Impact reduced; oncall will keep monitoring. Next update in 20m or on new developments. :white_check_mark:
ashwin: handing off to evening oncall @alexa in 30m. I'll leave runbook notes: commands we ran, prefixes touched, provider ticket 556732.
alexa: taking handoff. thanks @ashwin. I'll keep the watch and escalate if we see >5% loss again.
peering-team: provider sent initial BGP dump via secure link. I'll analyze and share suspicious origin changes.
jia: closing loop on metrics: dashboards show egress churn QPS back to baseline and no new NXDOMAIN flood. marking mitigations as successful for now.
alexa: posting status page now and tagging customers where required. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
